denounce: { correct: "win", wrong: "forfeit", from_round: 3, requires_evidence: true }

edits.find: From round 3, once per game, you may spend 1 AP to name the player you believe is The Enemy.
edits.replace: From round 3, once per game, you may spend 1 AP to name the player you believe is The Enemy — but only a player you have **evidence** against: you have seen their objective, they have been revealed, or you have seen a Forbidden Item in their hand (honest players take those too, to keep them from The Enemy — evidence is not proof).

rationale: Train runs: most games are decided by a round-3 denunciation (blind guesses, or an Enemy exposed by entering the Temple early); requiring evidence alone hands the Enemy its time-limit win (12-16 of 24) because honest objectives don't finish in 10 rounds, and pacing alone changes nothing while the lottery ends games first. They are one mechanism: pace the honest goals to the clock (12 rounds, Explorer 5, Builder 4) AND make deduction real (the Temple admits the Enemy only with the Amulet and the Tome; denouncing needs evidence).
